key_insight: ProofTrace reveals structural signatures of AI-generated proofs that differ from changes caused by AI rewording alone.
engineering_relevance: Graph-based analysis of proof organization could complement text-based detectors when assessing substantive AI involvement in mathematical papers.
method: Construct five cohorts totaling 8,281 papers, including matched papers addressing the same research problems.
Represent each paper as a graph of immediate proof support and extract interpretable structural features.
Analyze feature projections, test structural signatures under controls, and evaluate detection robustness to AI rewording.
evidence_signal: AI-generated proofs show fewer externally cited results, greater reliance on intermediate conclusions, and altered connectivity; detection of disclosed substantive AI use remains stable under AI rewording while text-based detector performance declines sharply.
watch_item: Potentially incomplete AI-use disclosures limit confidence in cohort labels and detection results.
paper_title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?
